# Import pkgs 

```{r}
# Load or install the `pacman` package to streamline package management
if (!require(pacman)) install.packages("pacman")

# Load required packages using pacman::p_load
pacman::p_load(
  # broom,         # Convert model outputs to tidy tibbles
  boot, # Bootstrapping
  tidyverse, # Core data science packages (ggplot2, dplyr, etc.)
  glue, # String interpolation
  here, # File paths relative to project root
  # purrr,         # Functional programming tools
  # estimatr,      # Robust linear regression and related estimators
  # effectsize,    # Calculate and interpret effect sizes
  # sandwich,      # Robust standard errors for model objects
  # ggrepel,       # Improved text label placement in ggplot2
  patchwork, # Combine ggplots into multi-panel layouts
  # ggpubr,        # Publication-ready ggplot enhancements
  # corrplot,      # Visualize correlation matrices
  # corrr,         # Tidy correlation workflows
  # correlation,   # Bayesian and frequentist correlation testing
  # callr,         # Run R code in a separate R session
  modelsummary, # Beautiful tables for regression results
  # confintr,      # Confidence intervals for statistical measures
  tinytable, # Lightweight table creation for reports
  # sf,            # Simple features for spatial data
  statebins, # Tile grid maps of the U.S.
  # RColorBrewer,  # Color palettes
  arrow # For reading/writing Apache Parquet files
)

# Load tidylog to get informative messages from dplyr workflows
library("tidylog", warn.conflicts = FALSE)

# Install and load stdidx (standardized indices) from GitHub
devtools::install_github("graemeblair/stdidx")
library(stdidx)

# Option to display effect size symbols (e.g., ∂, β)
options(es.use_symbols = TRUE)

# Source custom utility functions
source(here("functions", "utils.r"))

# Set default ggplot2 theme globally
ggplot2::theme_set(custom_theme())
```

# Import data 


```{r}
# Load key processed datasets from disk for summary and visualization.
# These include:
# - Second datasets: cnty/zcta_counts_cov (degree of civic opportunity)
# - Third datasets: cnty/zcta_civic_org_type (type of civic opportunity)

# County-level summary: 3,281 counties × 23 variables
cnty_counts_cov <- read_csv(here("data_outputs", "cnty_counts_cov.csv"))
dim(cnty_counts_cov) # 3,281 rows × 23 variables

# ZIP-level summary: 30,988 ZIP codes × 23 variables
zcta_counts_cov <- read_csv(here("data_outputs", "zcta_counts_cov.csv"))
dim(zcta_counts_cov) # 30,988 rows × 23 variables)
```

```{r}
## The third datasets (type of civic opportunity)

# County-level type classification: 29,687 rows × 5 columns
cnty_civic_org_type <- read_csv(here("data_outputs", "cnty_civic_org_type.csv"))
dim(cnty_civic_org_type) # 29,687 rows × 5 columns

# ZIP-level type classification: 150,162 rows × 5 columns
zcta_civic_org_type <- read_csv(here("data_outputs", "zcta_civic_org_type.csv"))
dim(zcta_civic_org_type) # 150,162 rows × 5 columns
```

# Summary of the datasets

```{r}
# Count unique counties represented in the third ddatasets 
length(unique(cnty_civic_org_type$FIPS)) # 3,124
# Count unique ZIP codes represented in the third datasets
length(unique(zcta_civic_org_type$ZCTA)) # 25,635

# For counties: calculate the proportion where the primary org category is "Social" or "Religious"
cnty_civic_org_type %>%
  select(FIPS, primary_org_cat) %>%    # Focus on one row per county and its dominant class
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(so_or_re = ifelse(str_detect(primary_org_cat, "Social|Reli"), 1, 0)) %>%  # Flag if dominant class matches pattern
  summarize(so_or_re_pct = mean(so_or_re, na.rm = TRUE))  # Share of counties with social or religious orgs dominant (~80%)

# For ZIPs: same procedure ??? compute proportion with “Social” or “Religious” as dominant category
zcta_civic_org_type %>%
  select(ZCTA, primary_org_cat) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(so_or_re = ifelse(str_detect(primary_org_cat, "Social|Reli"), 1, 0)) %>%
  summarize(so_or_re_pct = mean(so_or_re, na.rm = TRUE))  # Result: ~61%
```

# Description

## The first datasets 

### Table 5 

```{r}
################################################################################
# Table 5
################################################################################

# Generate a summary table of normalized civic opportunity metrics (mean + 95% CIs) at the county level

# Step 1: Precompute mean and 95% confidence intervals
ci_stats_cnty <- cnty_counts_cov %>%
  summarise(across(
    c(
      civic_org_sum_normalized, civic_opp_sum_normalized,
      volunteer_sum_normalized, membership_sum_normalized,
      take_action_sum_normalized, events_sum_normalized
    ),
    ~ {
      m <- mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
      se <- sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(.x)))
      lower <- m - 1.96 * se
      upper <- m + 1.96 * se
      sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", m, lower, upper)
    }
  )) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Mean [95% CI]")

# Step 2: Use datasummary_df to format the table
datasummary_df(
  ci_stats_cnty,
  output = "latex",
  fmt = 2,
  title = "County-Level Civic Opportunity Indicators"
) %>%
  save_tt(
    here("tables", "table5.tex"),
    overwrite = TRUE
  )
```

### Figure 2

```{r}
################################################################################
# FIGURE 2
################################################################################

# Bind county and ZIP-level summary data for plotting
# `civic_opp_index` is used to harmonize across geographic levels
binded_out <- bind_cnty_zcta_summaries(civic_opp_index, "Civic opportunity")

# Define list of 50 U.S. states (excludes DC and territories)
state_abb_50 <- state.abb

# Filter the dataset to include only those 50 states
binded_out <- binded_out %>%
  filter(state %in% state_abb_50)

#Bar Plot: Mean civic opportunity index by state and unit
bar_plot <- binded_out %>%
  mutate(state = factor(state)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = fct_reorder(state, avg),
    y = avg,
    fill = unit
  )) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = avg - 1.96 * se, ymax = avg + 1.96 * se),
    width = 0.3,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Average civic opportunity index",
    fill = "Unit"
  )

# Statebins Map: Visual summary using U.S. tile grid
statebin_plot <- binded_out %>%
  ggplot(aes(state = state, fill = avg)) +
  geom_statebins() +
  facet_wrap(~unit) + # Separate facets for counties vs ZIPs
  theme_statebins() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0),
    plot.margin = margin(30, 30, 30, 30)
  ) +
  labs(fill = "Average civic opportunity index")

# Combine plots
combined_plot <- bar_plot + statebin_plot + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")

combined_plot

# Save combined figure as PNG
ggsave(
  filename = here("plots", "figure2.png"),
  plot = combined_plot,
  width = 15,
  height = 10
)

ggsave(
  filename = here("plots", "figure2.jpg"),
  plot = combined_plot,
  width = 15,
  height = 10,
  dpi = 300
)
```

## The second datasets 

```{r}
# Combine county and ZIP-level datasets into a long-format summary
# Only keep distinct unit-category combinations

sd_binded_out <- bind_rows(
  cnty_civic_org_type %>%
    filter(!is.na(primary_org_cat)) %>%
    select(FIPS, primary_org_cat) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    group_by(primary_org_cat) %>%
    count() %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(freq = n / sum(n)) %>% # Calculate relative frequency per category 
    mutate(unit = "County"),
  
  zcta_civic_org_type %>%
    filter(!is.na(primary_org_cat)) %>%
    select(ZCTA, primary_org_cat) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    group_by(primary_org_cat) %>%
    count() %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(freq = n / sum(n)) %>%
    mutate(unit = "Zipcode")
)
```

### Figure 3 

```{r}
################################################################################
# FIGURE 3
################################################################################

# Create bar plot comparing frequencies of dominant org types by unit (County vs ZIP)
sd_binded_out %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(primary_org_cat, freq), y = freq, fill = unit)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Proportion",
    fill = "Unit"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(freq, accuracy = 1)),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
    vjust = -0.5
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.border = element_blank(), # Remove the border around the plot
    axis.line = element_blank(), # Remove the axis lines
    axis.ticks = element_blank(), # Remove the axis ticks
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12), # Optional: Adjust x-axis text size
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12) # Optional: Adjust y-axis text size
  ) # Adjust `vjust` for vertical positioning of labels

ggsave(here("plots", "figure3.png"),
  height = 10,
  width = 10
)

ggsave(
  filename = here("plots", "figure3.jpg"),
  width = 15,
  height = 10,
  dpi = 300
)
```
